column5: Comment Text
Is this actually real? I've seen so many fake campaigns online and honestly I don't know what to believe anymore. Has anyone verified this?

I was wary too but I checked the page properly. There are actual MRI scans posted in the updates, Salford Royal is named as the hospital, and the cost breakdown goes into detail for each treatment. it's nothing like those generic pages with just a sad story and a donate button
my colleague's daughter had dendritic cell therapy at the same clinic in Germany for breast cancer two years ago. the clinic is real. I've donated £15

I work in oncology research. the treatment protocol described here is consistent with what's offered at several German immunotherapy centres. the costs listed are in the right range too. I'm satisfied enough to donate

Lost my dad to a GBM in 2023. He was 54. There was nothing beyond standard chemo and radiotherapy. If dendritic cell therapy had been available and funded he might still be here. Donated everything I could spare. Please share this even if you can't give

so sorry for your loss. my uncle had the same diagnosis. 11 months from diagnosis to the end. the fact that a treatment now exists that could change outcomes but isn't funded by the NHS is heartbreaking
my mum passed from a brain tumour too. reading Grace's story brought it all back. at least now there is something beyond the standard pathway. donated

I'm a junior doctor in neurology. I've read the study they reference (Human Vaccines & Immunotherapeutics 2025). The 68% increase in median overall survival is real and specifically relevant for IDH-wildtype GBM which is what Grace has. The tragedy is NICE approval could take another 3-5 years. She doesn't have that time
this is what people need to understand. it's not that the treatment doesn't work. it's that the regulatory system hasn't caught up yet. real people die waiting for approval
exactly. the bureaucracy is literally the barrier between life and death here. it's disgraceful

21 years old and studying medicine at Manchester. she wanted to become a doctor to help people and now she's the patient. that quote about every donation being time she gets to keep living absolutely destroyed me. done ✅
that line got me too. donated and shared. come on people
done and shared. if everyone who scrolls past this today gives just £5 she'd hit her target within the week. takes 30 seconds
as a mum of a 19 year old daughter this terrifies me beyond words. you just never think it could be your child. donated and shared in our school parents WhatsApp
same here. I held my daughter extra tight after reading this. donated £10
the NHS won't fund a treatment with published clinical evidence because of bureaucratic approval timelines. meanwhile she has months not years. this country should be ashamed. donated £30
NICE classification as 'experimental' can drag on for 5+ years even with positive trial data. Grace doesn't have 5 years. that's why Germany is the only option right now
small donation from Birmingham but sending all the love and strength in the world. stay fighting Grace 💪
my wife and I both donated. we lost a close friend to this exact cancer last year. age 38, two young kids. if there's even a chance this treatment extends her life she absolutely deserves to try it

what convinced me was visiting the page and seeing the cost breakdown. it's not just 'give us money'. they've itemised exactly what each treatment costs — dendritic cells, proton beam, travel, everything. that level of transparency matters when there's so many fakes out there
that's what convinced me as well. plus the medical updates with dates and actual results. this isn't some mystery patient, it's properly documented
done 💚 shared on my story too. come on everyone even a fiver helps
donated in memory of my brother who we lost to brain cancer in 2024. he was 41. go get that treatment Grace. beat this thing
whoever is reading the comments and thinking about donating — just do it. you genuinely won't miss £5 or £10 but added up it could help save her life. I donated £10 and it took less than a minute

I had a cancer diagnosis at 23. different type but I remember the terror of being told your life might be measured in months. the fact that a treatment exists and she just needs funding is so cruel. donated
